items.prompt: A secret was committed yesterday. What does adding its filename to .gitignore accomplish?

options.text: It erases the secret from every historical commit
options.why: Ignore rules do not rewrite existing history.

options.text: It revokes the credential at its issuing service
options.why: Credential revocation is a separate security action.

options.text: It does not remove a tracked secret or revoke it
options.why: Treat exposure separately and rotate/revoke as appropriate.

options.text: It makes the existing secret safe to publish publicly
options.why: Ignoring does not make private material safe to disclose.

items.explanation: Ignore rules are not an exposure repair. A tracked secret can remain in history and the credential may remain usable until revoked.
